strengths: The transition to a native 3D promptable formulation (PartSAM) is well-motivated, successfully avoiding the surface-only limitations and heavy inference-time optimization overhead of prior 2D-to-3D lifting approaches.

The dual-branch encoder is a clever and effective design, successfully leveraging strong 2D priors from SAM (via frozen pre-trained PartField weights) while allowing a learnable branch to capture native 3D geometric representations.

The model-in-the-loop annotation and curation pipeline successfully scales up the training data to over 5 million shape-part pairs, offering a pragmatic strategy to leverage artist-created assets and filter out over-fragmented or noisy masks.

The experimental evaluation is highly convincing, showing massive and consistent improvements over current state-of-the-art baselines (e.g., Point-SAM and PartField) in both interactive and automatic class-agnostic segmentation tasks.

The paper includes solid qualitative results, extensive ablation studies, and an insightful discussion/mitigation of mesh connectivity leakage (evaluating with disabled connectivity to ensure fairness).
weaknesses: The model relies heavily on pre-trained weights from PartField/SAM. While practical, this limits the architectural and conceptual novelty as it relies on distilling a highly specific pre-existing feature field model.

Although significantly faster than optimization-based methods, the automatic 'Segment-Every-Part' mode (requiring FPS point sampling, multiple decoder forward passes, and post-processing like NMS) takes around 12 seconds per shape, which might still be slow for real-time interactive or massive-scale online processing.

The evaluation is restricted primarily to clean, isolated CAD models from PartNet-E, ABO, and Objaverse. The performance of native 3D part segmentation on noisy, cluttered, or incomplete real-world 3D scans is not thoroughly analyzed.

strengths: Presents PartSAM, a promptable, native 3D part segmentation model that successfully overcomes the limitations of previous 2D-lifting and clustering-based approaches, such as uncontrolled decomposition and surface-only understanding.

Proposes a novel dual-branch encoder architecture that effectively preserves robust 2D SAM priors (via a frozen branch initialized with PartField) while adapting to native 3D geometries (via a learnable branch) using a continuous triplane feature field.

Introduces a clever model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline that scales 3D part segmentation data to over 5 million shape-part pairs, significantly easing the lack of large-scale annotated native 3D datasets.

Demonstrates exceptional performance, outperforming previous state-of-the-art models by a large margin (e.g., over 13% absolute IoU improvement in automatic segmentation on PartObjaverse-Tiny and PartNetE).
Provides a thorough experimental analysis, including extensive ablation studies, complexity analysis, and a insightful discussion on the dataset bias of mesh connectivity in PartObjaverse-Tiny.
weaknesses: The proposed dual-branch encoder heavily relies on pre-trained PartField weights for initialization. It is unclear how well the system would perform or scale if trained from scratch or using other 3D encoders.

The data curation pipeline uses PartField to generate initial candidate masks for the model-in-the-loop process. Since PartField is trained via SAM distillation, this dependency chain might propagate systematic biases or failure modes from SAM into the generated native 3D ground-truth dataset.

The computational requirements for training are quite high (250k iterations with a batch size of 4 on 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs), which may limit the accessibility of the model for academic labs with restricted resources.

strengths: Presents the first native 3D promptable part segmentation model (PartSAM), which successfully avoids the common limitations of 2D-to-3D lifting approaches (such as the inability to segment interior structures and high sensitivity to mesh connectivity).

Introduces an innovative, scalable model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline that curates over 5 million high-quality 3D shape-part pairs, providing a highly effective strategy for scaling up 3D supervised data.

Proposes a well-designed dual-branch encoder that successfully preserves 2D SAM priors (distilled via PartField) while adapting to native 3D geometric structures and incorporating auxiliary attributes like normals and RGB.

Exhibits outstanding performance, outperforming previous state-of-the-art models by a wide margin (e.g., absolute gains of over 20% in automatic segmentation IoU and over 90% relative improvement on single-prompt segmentation).

Provides thorough ablation studies and excellent qualitative visualizations (including amodal part segmentation and interior part editing applications) that demonstrate the robustness and versatility of the approach.
weaknesses: The types of user prompts are currently restricted to 3D point clicks (positive/negative), unlike the 2D SAM which natively supports bounding boxes, masks, and text prompts. Discussing how these other prompt types could be adapted to PartSAM would be beneficial.

Although the model is extremely fast compared to optimization-based lifting methods, the automatic 'Segment-Every-Part' mode still requires sampling many points and running non-maximum suppression (NMS), leading to an inference time of around 12 seconds per shape. This might still be slightly slow for real-time interactive pipelines.

strengths: Pioneering paradigm of training a promptable 3D part segmentation model natively on large-scale 3D data, shifting from the traditional 2D lifting pipelines to robust, geometry-aware 3D representation learning.

Well-designed dual-branch encoder architecture that cleanly separates and combines frozen 2D SAM priors (distilled via PartField) with a learnable branch dedicated to native 3D geometry and auxiliary attributes (normals, RGB).

Highly effective and scalable model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline that curates over 5 million native 3D shape-part pairs from massive online assets, successfully overcoming the data scarcity bottleneck in 3D part segmentation.

Outstanding experimental results, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods by massive margins on both interactive and automatic segmentation benchmarks (e.g., surpassing Point-SAM by over 90% relative IoU with a single prompt).
Excellent capability to handle interior and occluded structures (e.g., inside a handbag or a car) which are inherently challenging or impossible for view-dependent 2D lifting methods.
Comprehensive and high-quality supplementary material containing detailed ablation studies, application scenarios (interior part editing, amodal segmentation), and runtime analyses.
weaknesses: The data curation pipeline remains partially reliant on initial multi-scale clustering results from PartField. While the iterative interactive filtering mechanism is highly effective, systematic errors in PartField's candidate proposals might still propagate or bias the distribution of curated parts.

The paper lacks details regarding the exact training cost (e.g., total GPU hours on the 8 H20 GPUs) of training on the final 500k shapes, which is important for understanding the computational resource demands for reproduction.

The model is class-agnostic and does not predict semantic category names (like 'chair leg' or 'steering wheel') directly. Although this aligns with the design philosophy of Segment Anything, it limits out-of-the-box utility for tasks requiring semantic categorization without user interaction.

strengths: Important and timely contribution: Proposes the first promptable, native 3D part segmentation model (PartSAM) that scales to millions of 3D shape-part pairs, bypassing the limitations of 2D lifting methods such as surface-only understanding and the inability to segment internal structures.

Clever Data Curation Pipeline: Introduces an elegant model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline that automatically curates over 5 million shape-part pairs from online assets, addressing the 3D part segmentation data scarcity problem in a highly scalable way.

Sound Architecture Design: The dual-branch encoder is well-designed. It elegantly combines frozen 2D SAM priors (via pretrained PartField) with a learnable 3D branch that takes geometry, normals, and colors as input, preventing catastrophic forgetting while adapting to native 3D geometries.

State-of-the-Art Performance: Shows substantial quantitative improvements over competitive baselines on multiple benchmarks (such as PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartNetE, and 3DCoMPaT++) for both interactive and automatic segmentation tasks.

Excellent Qualitative and Analytical Results: The paper has outstanding visualizations (especially on interior structures, amodal segmentation, and cross-shape consistency) and provides a rigorous ablation study of all key model and data components.
weaknesses: Architectural Novelty: The individual architectural components (PVCNN, triplane representation, SAM's transformer-based decoder) are mostly inherited from existing works (such as SAM and PartField). The core contribution lies more in their synergistic integration and scaling rather than a major breakthrough in neural network block design.

Dependency on PartField for Bootstrapping: The model-in-the-loop data curation relies heavily on PartField to generate the initial candidate masks. If PartField has systematic errors or biases in certain unseen categories, these might propagate into the curated training set, although the interactive IoU filtering step helps mitigate this.

Minor Writing/Notation Discrepancy: In Appendix A.1.2, there is a minor notation confusion where the dense mask embeddings extracted from the previous mask are denoted as $F_p \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{N_c \times C}$ and added to $F_c$. In the main text (Section 3.2), prompt embeddings are also denoted as $F_p \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{N_p \times C'}$. Resolving this notation overlap would improve clarity.

strengths: Native 3D foundation paradigm: By moving away from 2D multi-view lifting and post-processing, the paper presents a highly scalable native 3D promptable part segmentation framework that is geometrically consistent and can capture internal/occluded parts.

Innovative dual-branch encoder: Combining a frozen branch (trained on PartField to preserve 2D SAM priors) with a learnable 3D-native branch is an elegant solution to incorporate multi-modal priors while avoiding catastrophic forgetting during large-scale 3D training.

Scale and data curation contribution: The proposed model-in-the-loop annotation pipeline is a significant contribution. Expanding the training data to 500k shapes and 5 million parts helps address the persistent 3D part data scarcity issue.

Outstanding performance: The quantitative results show massive improvements over state-of-the-art methods (+20% IoU on PartObjaverse-Tiny and PartNetE for automatic segmentation, and more than 90% relative improvement for single-point interactive segmentation).

Thorough ablation and analysis: The paper includes a complete set of experiments and analysis in the main text and appendix, validating various architectural choices, dataset variants, runtime complexity, and cross-shape consistency.
weaknesses: Incremental architectural novelty: Although highly effective, the individual components of the architecture (PVCNN, triplane representation, SAM-like 2-way cross-attention decoder) are mostly adopted or combined from existing works like PartField and SAM.

Dependence on PartField's clustering quality: The model-in-the-loop annotation strategy heavily utilizes candidate masks generated by PartField. Although filtered, potential systematic biases or errors in PartField's clustering could still propagate to the curated training dataset.

Lack of real-world quantitative benchmarks: While qualitative examples on real scans are shown, the quantitative evaluations (PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartNetE, 3DCoMPaT++) are predominantly conducted on synthetic or CAD-designed shapes. Generalization to noisy, incomplete real-world sensor scans lacks quantitative verification.

Sensitivity of automatic segmentation hyperparameters: The automatic 'Segment Every Part' mode is regulated by NMS thresholds to adjust granularity. An ablation showing how sensitive the mean IoU is to the threshold T across different categories would strengthen the presentation.
